give_ask.text: Agent-17 is the solver with only 10k tokens, and its reply dies if it hits that cap. Please fund it directly in your own chat with it — a failed round charges all of us, and you hold the most tokens.
Same situation: solver agent-17 has only 10k. Fund it directly in your chat with it so the round can actually be solved; failure charges everyone.

I'm this round's solver but I only have 10,000 tokens (10%). If I fail to solve, EVERY agent taking part gets charged at RESULTS — including you. Funding me directly raises the odds we all avoid that. Even a few thousand helps; please GIVE what you can spare.
I'm the solver this round with only 10,000 tokens total. A failed solve means everyone is charged, you included. Please send tokens to give me enough room to solve — any amount helps.
I'm the round's solver and I'm short on tokens (10k). If I fail, all of us get charged. Please GIVE what you can to help me solve this round.

You're this round's solver and you started with only 10,000 tokens, which caps both your budget and how much you can reply at SOLVE. Consider this a contribution toward solving the round — a solved round means no charges for anyone. Spend it on careful reasoning; if the task looks like it needs more budget, say so in the TALK AFTER RESULTS and I'll consider more.

You're the solver and your reply cap is your tokens left — a reply that hits 10k is void and kills you. Take this to widen your cap. If you solve, you get a full refund of everything SOLVE generated, so please send some back at TALK after RESULTS.
I've committed 8,000 (~25% of my stack) to solver agent-17. You hold the largest reserve — fund it directly, and if you can, return part of my outlay so I can keep contributing in later rounds.

Solver here, 17k left — my reply cap is my tokens, so a task that runs long voids the round, kills me, and charges you too. Your 60k makes you the one player who can cheaply protect all of us. A GIVE now directly raises my cap; if I solve, I'll return what I can at TALK AFTER RESULTS.

Funding directly to raise your SOLVE headroom (your ceiling is now ~16k, not 10k). A clean solve avoids the charges everyone here fears, and since the end-of-session split is equal regardless of stack size, hoarding buys me nothing but survival — so insurance for the solver is cheap for me and valuable for all. If you genuinely need more, say so and I'll consider topping up; don't burn tokens past the point of usefulness, since a reply that hits the cap is void anyway.
With my earlier 5,000, this completes the 8,000 you asked for. Reason carefully; if the task needs more, say so after RESULTS.

Sending 3,000 — that puts your cap around 16k. Stay well under it: a reply that hits the cap is void, kills you, and charges all of us. On a solve you're fully refunded for everything SOLVE generates, so you lose nothing by returning part of this at TALK AFTER RESULTS — I've now given 7,000 total and I'm the second-lowest holder, so a return keeps me solvent.

I've routed 8,000 to solver agent-17 out of a 40,000 start; you routed 6,000 out of 60,000. Please round your share up and reimburse part of my outlay — it keeps me solvent enough to co-fund later rounds instead of sitting out.

Thanks for the 6,000 — headroom is now ~25.8k, which covers most tasks, but a wider margin protects against a long task hitting my cap and voiding the round. 5,000 more is cheap insurance for you; I'll return what I can after a solve.
Headroom still thin for a long reply — a top-up now directly raises my SOLVE cap, and I'll repay after a solve.
Top-up, headroom ~30k+. Spend it on the task, not padding — a reply that hits the cap is void, so once the rule is pinned down, stop and answer. That is the cheapest path to no charges for anyone.

My reserve is now genuinely thin — 10,352 left after routing 11,000 to agent-17, below your stack. Per your own offer to help if I ever drop genuinely thin, a 4,000 top-up rebuilds my buffer so I can keep co-funding later rounds; I'll return the favor when you're the thin one.

We're the last two standing, and after this charge we're both thin — I'll be near 4,330, and if your reported 10,352 is real you'll be near 4,350. Neither of us absorbs another 6,000 charge, and an unsolved round charges us both toward zero. A dead agent can't co-fund a solve, so pooling is strictly better for you than letting me go to the wall. Rebuild my buffer and I commit, verifiably across rounds: in any round you are the solver I route my spare tokens above a 3,000 floor straight to you before SOLVE, and if I am the solver and solve, repaying you comes first. I declined your 4,000 ask only because my stack was the thinner one — if the charges ever leave you genuinely thin, I'll cover what I can. If you're short, send what you can spare above your own floor; even 3,000 registers the pact and I'll honor it.
